ig_caption:
The Sicilian is Black's most popular answer to 1.e4, and it grows with you. Here it is at three levels.

At 800: 1...c5 fights for the d4 square from the side, and makes a lopsided game where both players can win.
At 1200: in the Open Sicilian White gets quick development, but Black is left with two centre pawns against one and an open c-file.
At 1600: the Najdorf, 5...a6, a small pawn move that keeps White's pieces off b5 and gets Black ready for ...e5 or ...b5.
And if White plays 2.c3 instead, 2...d5 is a simple, sound reply.

slides.title: The Sicilian
slides.sub: ONE MOVE, THREE WAYS TO SEE IT

slides.title: At 800: the idea
slides.take: Black doesn't copy White with 1...e5. The c-pawn fights for the d4 square from the side, and the game gets lopsided.
slides.edge: Keep it simple: bring out your knights, play ...d6 or ...e6, and keep your queen at home for now.

slides.title: At 1200: the trade
slides.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3
slides.take: White gets quick development and room to attack. In return Black swapped a side pawn for White's d-pawn.
slides.edge: So Black has two centre pawns against one, plus an open c-file for the rook. That's Black's long-term edge.

slides.title: At 1600: the Najdorf
slides.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6
slides.take: A small pawn move with big jobs. It keeps White's knight and bishop off b5.
slides.edge: It also gets Black ready for ...e5, kicking the d4 knight, or ...b5, pushing on the queenside.

slides.title: If White plays 2.c3
slides.take: White wants to rebuild the centre with d4 next. 2...d5 hits back at once.
slides.edge: After 3.exd5 Qxd5 your queen is safe in the middle: White's pawn on c3 has taken the knight's best square.
